scope: CBSE Class 6 Mathematics · Ganita Prakash · Chapter 10 · The Other Side of Zero
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 10 topic, an existing Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action and an observable mastery criterion. Integer comparison must use number-line order rather than unsigned digit size; zero must remain neither positive nor negative; opposite integers must be equally distant from zero; addition and subtraction must preserve signed direction, opposite-number and zero-pair meaning; and contextual signed quantities must declare and retain a reference zero and sign convention without treating every negative value as inherently bad.

scenarios.need: Learner compares negative integers by unsigned digit size and concludes that -8 is greater than -3 because 8 is greater than 3.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: comparing negative integers by digit size alone
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Place fictional positive and negative integers on a paper number line, compare each pair by left-right position, and explain why the integer farther to the right is greater even when its unsigned digit is smaller.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly orders six new mixed-sign integer sets and justifies every negative-negative comparison from number-line position rather than digit size.

scenarios.need: Learner labels zero as positive or negative, or confuses numerical order with distance from zero.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a fictional number-line table to classify integers as negative, zero or positive, then separately record each value's distance from zero and compare values such as -6 and -2 without replacing order by absolute distance.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Classifies zero correctly as neither positive nor negative and distinguishes signed order from distance-to-zero reasoning in five new examples.

scenarios.need: Learner places opposite integers at unequal distances from zero or treats opposites as merely numbers with different signs.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: placing opposite numbers at unequal distances from zero
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Mark fictional integers and their opposites on a symmetric paper number line, measure equal step distances from zero, and identify the opposite of each labelled value including the special case of zero.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Constructs five correct opposite pairs at equal distances from zero, identifies zero as its own opposite, and detects an intentionally misplaced opposite point.

scenarios.need: Learner adds absolute values and guesses the final sign instead of tracking signed direction or combining positive and negative quantities correctly.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: adding absolute values and guessing the sign
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Solve fictional mixed-sign additions using directed number-line moves or positive/negative counters, record the starting point and each signed movement, and check the final location before writing the result.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Solves six new mixed-sign additions correctly and explains the result using signed movement or cancellation rather than unsigned addition followed by a guessed sign.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes subtraction always makes a number smaller and cannot explain why subtracting a negative can move a value to the right.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: assuming subtraction always makes a number smaller
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Model fictional integer subtractions on a paper number line by rewriting subtraction as adding the opposite, then compare the starting and ending positions for cases that increase, decrease or leave the value unchanged.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Solves and explains five new signed subtractions, including subtracting a negative, and correctly predicts whether each result is greater than or less than the starting value.

scenarios.need: Learner thinks adding or removing a positive-negative zero pair changes the represented integer.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: treating zero pairs as changing the represented value
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Represent fictional integers with paper positive and negative tokens, add several matched positive-negative pairs, verify that the net value is unchanged, and use zero pairs to make a subtraction model possible without altering the starting value.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses zero pairs correctly in four new token models, preserves the represented starting value, and explains why each added positive-negative pair contributes net zero.

scenarios.need: Learner drops the sign when interpreting temperature, elevation, floor or fictional credit/debit values, or assumes every negative value means something bad.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: dropping the sign when interpreting a result
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: For fictional temperatures, elevations, floors and account-change examples, state the reference zero and sign meaning first, calculate each signed change, then translate the final signed integer back into words without treating negative as a universal judgement.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Interprets six new signed-context results with the correct sign, reference and units, including at least two cases where a negative value is descriptive rather than inherently bad.

scenarios.need: Learner mixes sign conventions across a multi-step problem or needs to complete signed-number reasoning without cloud tutoring, personal data collection or remote monitoring.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: mixing sign conventions without stating the reference
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached Kiki text, locally available Chapter 10 prompts, paper and a pencil to define one fictional reference zero and sign convention, solve a multi-step signed-change sequence, check direction and magnitude, and explain the final value without any network-dependent tutoring or submission step.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes a new Chapter 10 signed-context sequence fully offline, keeps one consistent reference/sign convention through every step, verifies the result for direction and magnitude, and requires no real-child data or external communication.
